entries.claim: The shared result builder unconditionally adds `resultType` and `_meta` to legacy `initialize` responses, contradicting the compatibility promise that `initialize` is unchanged and older clients are served as before.
entries.failure_scenario: A client using an older initialize handshake and strict response deserialization sends `initialize` for `2025-06-18`. The response now contains two fields outside the legacy initialize result shape, so such a client rejects the handshake instead of proceeding. The same injection also affects every subsequent legacy result; there is no negotiated-version gate limiting the new envelope to `2026-07-28`.

counter_evidence.note: The two members on every result are the phase decision D-02 in .planning/phases/14/CONTEXT.md:16, taken on the spec: basic/index Result Responses makes resultType additive (an absent one is read as complete) and lets a JSON-RPC result carry any member, and every MCP schema revision declares Result with _meta and an open index signature, so _meta on a 2025-06-18 initialize result is inside the shape that revision defines, and a client that rejects it violates its own schema. The changelog sentence the finding reads as a promise refers to the handshake: the initialize method, its negotiation and PROTOCOL_VERSIONS are unchanged (D-08), and the same entry states two lines earlier that every result carries the two members. No negotiated-version gate was omitted; one shape on both eras is the decision, and D-02 names the condition under which it is revisited. AC6 passed live on Claude Code 2.1.302.
